newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BISHOPS CONDEMN LARRY FLINT FILM POSTER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BISHOPS CONDEMN LARRY FLINT FILM POSTER.

text.p: Polish Roman Catholic bishops have condemned as criminal and sacriligious a poster advertising the Hollywood film "The People vs Larry Flynt," which depicts a man in a crucifiction pose on a woman's pelvis.

Cardinal Jozef Macharski in the southern city of Krakow asked the local prosecutor's office earlier this week to investigate whether or not the distribution of the poster was a criminal act, newspapers reported.

"Contents of this poster offend religious feelings and are against the freedom of conscience and religion, which violates articles...of the criminal code," Macharski wrote to the prosecutor in a letter published by the Zycie daily.
Under the Polish law, a person offending religious feelings can face up to two years in prison or a fine.
The cardinal's letter followed a vocal campaign by pro-church groups, which demanded that the poster be banned in the predominantly Roman Catholic country.
Right-wing youth have teared down the posters throughout the country and blurred it with paint.
The Krakow prosecutors spokeswoman Malgorzata Wilkosz-Sliwa said no decision had so far been taken whether to launch a probe against the poster.
The controvercial poster has been rejected by the Motion Picture Association of America and became subject to vocal protests in Italy, France, Germany and Switzerland.
It advertises the movie about the life of the American pornography publishing king, which won the "Golden Bear" for best picture at the 47th Berlin Film festival last month.
The film, directed by Milos Forman, has also won two Oscar nominations.
The church's protest action two years ago against a British movie "The Priest," which depicted a homosexual cleric, has led to its strong showing at the box-office.
